# Spiritual
 Translation
 of the Chapter
 of
 the Dragon


---


**
¶2:**
 There
 is no
 ruling
 fals
ity in the natural
 person poss
essing fourteen modes
 of domin
ion, as those
 who hold
 external knowledge
 without interior
 understanding have
 declared
. Rather
, this is a teaching
 concerning
 spiritual
 states
.
 It was spoken from
 a
 condition
 of innocence and
 purity of doctrine. Those
 who possessed
 only
 external
 knowledge did not compreh
end that
 all their words,
 as
 set
 down
,
 express
 spiritual re
alities through
 correspondence.

**¶3:**
 This
 is how the external
 natural mind —
 which
 in
 its
 tot
ality is r
eckoned as
 a living
 fals
ity governing
 from
 self
hood — is to
 be understood
. The dragon is the ruling
 principle
 of the prop
rium, the self
-derived life
 of the natural person
. The fourteen
 governing
 powers
 distributed
 throughout
 this
 fals
ity are as
 follows.


**¶4:** The seven
 modes
 of perception belonging
 to the cognitive
 region
 of
 the natural
 mind are these
: the
 two fac
ulties of intellectual
 sight
, by
 which one app
rehends ideas
; the two faculties of ob
edient reception
, by which one receives tru
ths or
 fals
ities through
 hearing
; the two faculties of interior disc
ernment, by which one perce
ives the
 quality
 of what
 approaches
 the spirit
; and
 the faculty of appet
itive selection
, by which one distingu
ishes and
 receives
 varied
 del
ights that
 present
 themselves in every form of
 experience
.

**¶5:** These
 are the seven governing
 powers
 of the prop
rium's
 fals
ity that
 operate
 through
 the higher
 or
 intellectual
 region
 of the natural
 person
. And
 there
 are likewise
 seven governing powers in
 the lower
 or v
olitional and
 corpor
eal region
 —
 seven
 appet
ites and drives
 corresponding
 to those
 above
. The
 seven
 modes
 of perception
 above
,
 united
 with the seven modes
 of appetite below, complete
 the
 fourteen powers
 by
 which the fals
ity of self
hood exercises
 total
 dominion over the
 natural
 person.

**¶6:**
 The
 five interior conce
alment
-places,
 spoken
 of in
 the ancient
 teaching, where this
 ruling
 falsity g
athers its
 strength
 and from
 which it emer
ges into
 activity
, are these: the first
 is the faculty
 of persu
asive speech, through
 which fals
ity is expressed and
 propag
ated; the second is the faculty of
 spiritual resp
iration, the thought
-life itself
,
 which
 when
 corrupted serves
 fals
ity; the third is the will
, the in
most
 seat
 of self-love, where
 evil
 enth
rones itself; the fourth is the faculty
 of interior
 discrimination
 among
 aff
ections, which
 when
 perv
erted can
 no
 longer distinguish good
 from evil; the fifth is the living
 truth
 of
 faith that
 circulates through all these
 faculties —
 which
,
 when prof
aned, carries
 corruption
 everywhere
 throughout
 the spirit
.
 When
 the
 fals
ity of selfhood looks
 out
ward from
 these conce
aled
 seats and manif
ests its
 nature
 through
 both
 the
 intellectual
 and the
 volitional regions, it wages spiritual
 combat
 by
 means
 of all
 fourteen
 powers
 at
 once
.

**¶7:**
 Whoever comes
 to recognize these
 powers
 together
 with the ruling
 falsity itself
 —
 which is the self
-derived thinking of the natural person
,
 the
 proprium — and eng
ages in
 spiritual combat against
 it, and
 prev
ails, and
 ext
inguishes its
 life within
 these
 fac
ulties:
 that
 person receives victory
 without suffering on
 the day of depar
ting from the
 natural state
 into
 spiritual life.

**¶8
:** Thus
 the
 complete
 teaching has
 been given concerning
 the fals
ity of
 self
hood that gov
erns the unre
generate person
 through
 its
 fourteen powers
 of
 dominion and five
 interior
 seats
,
 within
 which it lies
 concealed and hidden,
 and through which it perpet
ually
 en
acts its ruling
 love
.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Again, this is how this earth[ly body stands in regard] to it, as it is accounted a corporeal dragon [in its entirety.] I will instruct you [concerning it:] the dragon is this doctrine [of the thought] of the flesh [, the selfhood of the body;] also the fourteen heads that are distributed over the dragon are these.

The seven sense organs on the head of the body are the two of sight by which one sees; the two of sound by which one hears; the two of scent by which one smells; also the tongue [, the single organ of taste,] by which one selects, receiving there the different tastes that occur in every form.

These are the seven heads of the dragon, the seven sense organs that are on the upper part of the person; [and there are also seven] below. The seven of the torso are these: two [of the hands]; the two [of the feet; the belly; the organ of generation, which is the] ruler [of bodily desire; and the fundament. These correspond to] the seven heads that are above; so with the ones below they total and make fourteen heads of the dragon.

Conversely, the five dens about which they have spoken, where the dragon is congregated and protrudes, are these: the first is the tongue; the second is the lungs; the third is the heart; the fourth is the spleen; the fifth is the blood that dwells in them. Again, if it shall look out from them [and manifest its likeness and its power above and below, it wages war through] its fourteen heads.

Whoever will recognise them with the dragon, which is the thought of the body, and struggles with it and is victorious and kills it in them [, that person has conquered the dragon.] He receives the victory without suffering on the day of his coming forth.
So, behold, I have taught you of the dragon that exists with its fourteen heads and five dens, wherein it is concealed and hidden. It does through them [all the deeds of its des]ire all the time.

There is never a dragon
 in the flesh with fourteen heads, as
 the Magi say! Rather,
 this is a spiritual lesson. It was
 uttered in virginity [and p
urity of doctrine, but] the
 Magi did not understand [the meaning
, that] all their words that are
 written [therein are spiri]
tual
